#### The continuous query — stack and heap at every step

**What is being answered.** What a continuous query actually does to its sink, and why the sink contract is readable from the query.

Two lines carry the whole chapter. `if (bucketOf(EVENTS[i]) != W0) { continue }` is all of `TUMBLE(et, 120s)` — it reads `et` and never asks the time. `if (watermarkAfter(i) < W0 + WIN && fired == false) { continue }` is the emission moment, and neither 15 nor 12:04:06 appears in the SQL.

Step 4 prices the sink mismatch: the same two emissions give 19 into an UPSERT sink and 34 into an INSERT-only one. Every component is behaving correctly.

The animation steps through the code, holding each line long enough to read the STACK (call frames and their locals) and the HEAP (allocated arrays and objects) as they are AT THAT MOMENT. Expand any step to study it on its own.

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-system-memory/frames/step-01.svg" alt="Step 1: the bucket is read off the et column, and nothing else" width="980">

`bucketOf(EVENTS[3])` is 120, which is not W0 = 0, so row 3 is skipped. That one line is the whole of `TUMBLE(et, 120s)` — it reads `et` and never asks what time it is now.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 2 of 4</b> — the watermark decides the moment, and the engine emits</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-system-memory/frames/step-02.svg" alt="Step 2: the watermark decides the moment, and the engine emits" width="980">

`watermarkAfter(4)` is 185, no longer below 120, so the `continue` is skipped and the bucket emits `sum(ids)` = **15**. Neither 15 nor 12:04:06 appears anywhere in the query text — both come from this comparison.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 3 of 4</b> — id 7 arrives and the SAME row is written again</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-system-memory/frames/step-03.svg" alt="Step 3: id 7 arrives and the SAME row is written again" width="980">

`sink.rows[0] = 19` — an assignment, replacing 15. `writes` reaches 2 for one logical result, which is what "updating stream" means in practice: the sink is written more often than the answer changes meaning.

</details>
<details>
<summary><b>Step 4 of 4</b> — and an INSERT-only sink reads the two writes as two facts</summary>

<img src="../diagrams/anim/ch08-system-memory/frames/step-04.svg" alt="Step 4: and an INSERT-only sink reads the two writes as two facts" width="980">

The same two emissions, into a sink that adds: 15 + 19 = **34** for a window worth 19. The query, the engine and the sink are each behaving correctly. The mismatch is the sink's update mode against the query's — and that is decidable from the query text before any of this runs.
